To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Fos is involved in regulation of proenkaephlin and prodynorphine gene expression in the hippocampus.
the induction of FOS protein in the hippocampus during seizures is required for the subsequent induction of PEN and PDYN mRNAS.
the kainate-induced seizures in the rat hippocampal dentata elicits the induction of proenkeaphalin (PEN) and prodynorphin (PDYN) mRNAs, which is inhibited by an antisense oligo to the c-fos gene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of the regulation of gene expression, in this case the proenkepalin and prodynorphine genes in the hippocampus.
the mechanisms of regulation of gene expression of the opioid peptides, enkephalin and dynorphin.

the role of the transcription factor c-fos in the regulation of the expression of the proenkaeplalin (PEN) and prodynorfin (PDN) genes in the rat hippocampal dentrate gyrus during seizures induced by kainic aci.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Fos is involved in regulation of PENK and/or PDYN gene expression only in some brain regions and only under certain conditions.

the transcription factor CRE-BP (CREB) is the main factor regulating the expression of PENK and/or PDYN genes in the hippocampus, while Fos is the main transcription factor in the hypothalamus and striatum.
the mechanisms of the up-regulation in the hippocampi of the proenka- and prodynorphins are not identical to those operating in the striatum and the hypothalamus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Fos is a transcription factor that is involved in the regulation of PENK and/or PDYN gene expression, but the exact mechanisms and pathways of this regulation may differ in various brain regions.
CREB and Fos are both involved in regulation of PENK and/or PDYN gene expression.
Fos is involved in regulation of proenkaephlin gene expression in the hippocampus and in the striatum and in regulation of prodynorphin expression in the hypothalamus and in the striatun.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Fos may play a role in the mechanism of induction of PENK mRNA expression in the hippocampus during kainate-induced seizures.
the mechanisms triggering up-regulation of the PENK gene in the dentate may differ from those in the striatum.
Fos may play a role in the regulation of PENK and/or PDYN gene expression, which has not been previously demonstrated.
